items.en: The baby, curled up for lack of space, generally keeps their legs folded toward the chest while continuing to move regularly.
About 45 cm
Cantaloupe melon
Despite the reduced space, the baby’s movements and the changing shape of your belly usually remain noticeable.
Continuing to pay attention to the baby’s usual movements remains relevant right up until birth.
The baby keeps filling out, which will help them regulate their temperature once born. The available space in the uterus becomes more limited.
About 46.2 cm
Honeydew melon
More pronounced pelvic pressure may appear as the baby gradually descends.
Despite the limited space, the baby should continue moving with a regularity similar to previous weeks.
The lungs have generally matured enough to allow independent breathing, and the baby is able to suck and digest.
About 47.4 cm
Romaine lettuce
You may sometimes feel shorter of breath, as the uterus takes up a lot of space under the ribs.
Pregnancy is considered full term between week 37 and week 42.
The baby is considered mature enough to be born. The large majority of babies are now positioned head-down.
About 48.6 cm
Leek
A feeling of growing pelvic pressure is common as the baby engages in the pelvis.
From this week on, term is considered reached and birth can happen at any time.
The fine down that covered the skin has largely disappeared, and the intestines are accumulating meconium, the newborn’s first stool.
About 49.8 cm
Rhubarb stalk
Getting familiar with the signs of labor can be useful as birth approaches.
A scheduled birth, when considered without a medical indication, is generally not recommended before week 39.
The skin, previously thinner, has thickened and now protects the baby better. A protective coating, the vernix, also eases their passage during birth.
About 50.7 cm
Watermelon
Impatience and a certain amount of fatigue are common as the due date approaches.
The newborn’s blood circulation continues adjusting just after birth, which can temporarily give the hands or feet a slightly bluish tinge.
The baby is fully developed and ready to be born. The due date is an estimate: many births happen in the days surrounding it, before or after.
About 51.2 cm
Pumpkin
Waiting for signs of labor (regular contractions, water breaking) is common during this period.
Going slightly past the due date remains common and doesn’t necessarily mean there’s a problem; closer monitoring is generally offered.
The baby remains fully developed. Beyond the due date, closer monitoring is generally offered to check on the baby’s wellbeing.
The prolonged wait may come with increased fatigue and impatience.
Going past term generally leads to increased monitoring by the medical team.
